systems.name: creative-core
systems.description: The pure-Swift engines of a Mac-native creative suite: the FlareCore animation engine plus the shared CoreColor, CoreRaster, CoreAsset, CoreCatalog, CoreRender and CoreRenderMetal modules. Linux-safe, Foundation only, except CoreCatalog, which uses GRDB over the system SQLite, and CoreRenderMetal, which uses Metal on macOS and builds empty on Linux. The Mac apps live in other repos.

containers.name: FlareCore library
containers.description: The FlareCore Swift package (Sources/FlareCore). Value types only, Codable and Sendable, and nothing crashes on untrusted input.

components.name: Document and Command Engine
components.description: The document model (Document > Scene > Layer > Shape, keyframe tracks, fills, text shapes, ruler guides, the W1 layer masks and track mattes, text runs with paragraph and path-text styles and their text layout, colour and shape tracks, the swatch palette, metadata, frame labels) and its ModelError; LayerOwner, which addresses a scene's or a symbol's layer list; the Command protocol and CommandEngine with exact undo/redo, groups, coalescing, an undo depth limit and layer-scoped validation for single-layer commands; the CommandRegistry that decodes any command from a JSON envelope; the built-in command families (scene, layer, shape, text, keyframe, label, guide, swatch, metadata), with the stroke, path and duplicate-layer commands, scene canvas, rename and reorder; and the .flare v1 file format with validation. Every document change goes through a Command.

components.name: Geometry
components.description: 2D affine Matrix, the Transform (position, scale, rotation; scene space is y down) layers and instances use, axis-aligned Rect, vector Paths with line, quadratic and cubic segments and their affine transform, tight shape bounds, and point hit testing (even-odd and nonzero fill, strokes, through instances). The per-frame render list of a scene or symbol: one walk that gives the layer and instance tree exporters write and the flat paint-order items (matrix, multiplied opacity, inherited lock, address) the stage draws, each with its clips (its layer's and host layers' masks in scene space, in order, with mode, feather, opacity and inversion) and its track matte (the source's items and the matte kind, a hidden source listed only as a matte item, the source flagged); the queries over it (topmost hit with a tolerance, marquee, world bounds with stroke); and the path builders for rectangles, ellipses, polygons and stars. The path ops in PathOps/: an anchors view (corner, smooth and symmetric points with handles) that round-trips to Path; nearest point, insert, remove and convert an anchor; arc length, the point and tangent at a length, trim and dash; a stroke outlined into a fillable path for every join and cap; and union, subtract, intersect and exclude under either fill rule, refusing input past a vertex cap with tooComplex. Nothing here traps on non-finite input.

components.name: Timeline
components.description: Frame/time conversion, keyframe interpolation with binary-search segment lookup, easing curves (linear, cubic bezier, hold), sampling a layer's property values (and its colour and shape tracks) at a frame for rendering and export, and onion skin frames around the playhead.

components.name: Export
components.description: Exporters that turn a scene into other formats: one frame as an SVG document, a scene as a Lottie JSON document with animated position, scale, rotation and opacity, and gradient stop alpha, and the frame plan (numbers, times, pixel sizes, file names) for a numbered PNG sequence. Output is byte-stable and throws on non-finite values. W1 writers fill one seam file each: SVGExporter+Style (paint at the frame), SVGExporter+Text (each text shape as one <text>, laid out over the metrics the caller measures, FixedAdvances by default: runs as tspans with their font properties, lines at their layout baselines, alignment as text-anchor, justified lines as one x per Unicode scalar, each element on one line), SVGExporter+TextPath (type on a path as a textPath naming its path in defs, startOffset as a percentage, a flipped path written reversed), SVGExporter+Masks (layer masks as a clipPath and a luminance mask with feather as a Gaussian blur, track mattes as a mask holding the source layer; difference masks throw) and LottieExporter+Masks (masksProperties with mode, inv, o and x, track mattes as tt on the matted layer and td on its source directly above; feathered masks throw, since Lottie masks have no feather), LottieExporter+Tracks (animated properties, including colour, width and shape keys).

components.name: Import
components.description: Importers that read the vector formats export writes, its inverse, both built: SVGImport.scene reads an SVG document into one scene and LottieImport.document reads a Lottie JSON document into a document, each with byte, element, layer and depth caps, a typed ImportError and an ImportReport listing what was skipped. The SVG reader walks XMLTokens, the bounded, Linux-safe XML tokenizer (tags, attributes, text, entities; comments, declarations and CDATA skipped), reads path data with SVGPathData (every command, absolute and relative, arcs as cubics) and cascades fill, stroke, opacity and font properties from attributes and style with SVGStyle; it turns basic shapes and paths, with their transforms baked in, solid and gradient fills (href chains followed with a visited set), strokes, clip paths as layer masks and text as text shapes into one layer per top-level drawable, counting every other element and each reference cycle as skipped. The Lottie reader (LottieImport, with its animation half) turns shape and solid layers, their paths, rectangles, ellipses, fills, strokes, gradients and transforms into one scene, with keyframes (easings from the file's handles, holds) as position, scale, rotation, opacity, colour, stroke width and shape tracks, masks as layer masks and tt as track mattes, counting parents, expressions, keyed anchors, group transforms and other layer kinds as skipped. ImportNumber is the exact fast decimal path (Clinger's) that SVGPathData and the Lottie JSON reader try before Double(String).

components.name: Symbols
components.description: Reusable symbol definitions and their instances on layers: how an instance maps the host timeline onto the symbol's own timeline, the add/remove/rename/convert-to-symbol commands, the instance add, remove, move and playback commands, and the check that rejects symbols that contain themselves.

components.name: State Machine
components.description: Interactive state machines: states that play a frame range of a scene, transitions fired by named triggers, typed bool/number inputs with transition conditions, the issues query that lists every broken rule and unreachable state without throwing, the format-layer check over it that FlareFormat.validate runs, the machine, state, transition and input commands, and the player that steps a machine at run time.

containers.name: CoreColor library
containers.description: Shared color module (Sources/CoreColor): color spaces and conversions for every app. Linux-safe, Foundation only, no dependencies.

components.name: Color Spaces
components.description: Color3 and conversions between sRGB, linear sRGB, Display P3, XYZ D65 and OKLab through one shared transfer curve (public as TransferCurve, which CoreRaster's sRGB tone encoding uses); 8-bit display tables (DisplayTransfer: table decode and threshold encode for sRGB and Display P3); ColorError.

components.name: ICC Profiles
components.description: ColorProfile, an ICC matrix-and-curve profile as a plain value: RGB (nine colourants, three curves) or gray (its white point, one curve), colourants in XYZ relative to the D50 PCS already Bradford-adapted, curves as gamma, table or parametric (para types 0 to 4 with 1, 3, 4, 5 or 7 parameters); the built-in sRGB (para type 3), Display P3 and linear sRGB profiles have their colourants and parameters rounded to the s15Fixed16 grid, so a written built-in reads back ==. The ICC reader (ICCRead) bounds-checks every offset, size and count with no Int overflow: v2 or v4, display or input class, RGB or GRAY data space and an XYZ PCS; curv tags (0 entries identity, 1 a u8Fixed8 gamma, more a uInt16 table) and para tags; a desc or mluc description; colourants read as stored. Damaged bytes, a missing tag, a LUT-based profile (A2B or B2A tags without the matrix-and-curve tags), CMYK, Lab or another colour space, a Lab PCS, another class or version, and another curve or description type throw ColorError naming the cause. The ICC writer (ICCWrite) emits deterministic v4.3 display bytes (date and profile ID 0): header, tag table, each tag 4-byte aligned and zero-padded, tags with equal bytes shared; mluc desc, then for RGB a D50 wtpt, chad as the Bradford D65-to-D50 matrix, colourants and three TRCs, for gray its white in wtpt and kTRC; wrong value or curve counts, a value outside s15Fixed16 or u8Fixed8, a table under 2 entries or outside 0...1, a para type or count out of range and a size past uInt32 throw ColorError. ProfileTransform maps encoded colours through the D50 PCS: source curves, source colourants, linear Bradford adaptation when the two whites (where RGB 1, 1, 1 or gray 1 lands) differ, inverse target colourants, inverse target curves (tables by binary search, extended past 1); curves are odd-extended and nothing is clamped; a gray source reads the first component and a gray target writes r == g == b. Wrong counts, non-finite values, singular target colourants, a gray white with Y <= 0, a white with a zero cone response, an overflowing matrix and an uninvertible curve (a falling or flat table, gamma <= 0, para slope a <= 0 or linear slope c < 0) throw ColorError.

containers.name: CoreRaster library
containers.description: Shared raster module (Sources/CoreRaster): pixel buffers, compositing and image operations for Photo, Library and Halo. Linux-safe, Foundation only.

components.name: Pixel Buffer
components.description: PixelBuffer and RGBA: validated sizes, bounds-checked access, premultiply helpers; conversion to and from 8-bit sRGB or Display P3 display bytes through CoreColor's display tables, of the whole buffer or of one region without a crop copy; the tile grid for per-tile storage and paint, and TileDiff for tile-by-tile undo; RasterError.

components.name: Compositing
components.description: W3C blend modes and source-over compositing with opacity on premultiplied pixels, in place on the backdrop one row at a time (an opaque normal row at full opacity is copied in), with free functions that composite a copy. Compositing/ holds the W1 composites, such as compositing through a mask at its own offset.

components.name: Image Operations
components.description: Masks, resampling, crop, quarter turns and rotation by any angle with the straighten crop, blur, tone adjustments and histograms (levels, curves and histograms on linear or sRGB-encoded values) and cloning from an offset through a mask over PixelBuffer. W1/ declares the values the W1 engines share (AffineMatrix, ColorLUT, LayerEffect and the tone, matte, fill and gradient values), with no operations. Masks/ holds mask feathering, contours and mattes read from a buffer. Tone/ holds the color-family tone ops and the auto-tone suggestion. Effects/ holds the layer effects a PixelBuffer applies. Affine/ holds transforms through an AffineMatrix, flips and canvas padding. Fill/ holds flood fill by tolerance, colour range masks and raster gradient fills, with FillColor, the one colour distance flood fill and colour range share (Euclidean OKLab of the straight colours, alpha as a fourth axis). Heal/ holds the gradient-domain heal from an offset through a mask, seeded fill from surroundings (a patch search followed by a heal), dodge, burn and sponge tone dabs by TonalRange, and the SmudgeState brush state. Hash/ holds PerceptualHash, a 64-bit DCT hash of a buffer: resampled to 32 x 32 with the bilinear filter (which averages areas when shrinking), Rec. 709 luminance of the premultiplied values, so alpha composites over black, sRGB-encoded, a 2-D DCT-II, and one bit per coefficient (u, v) in 1...8 (the DC row and column dropped) set when it is above their median; distance is the popcount of the XOR, and the same buffer gives the same bits on every platform. It also holds DuplicateGroups, which puts ids whose hashes chain within a distance (clamped to 0...10, negative groups nothing, since past 10 random hashes start to chain) into groups of two or more, each id in one group, each group sorted by id and the list by first id, through a multi-index table over four 16-bit blocks and a union-find, near-linear in the number of hashes.

components.name: Layered Codecs
components.description: The suite's layered-file codecs, PSD and OpenRaster (ORA). LayeredImage, the neutral value: pixel layers with offset, opacity, blend mode, visibility, clipping and a placed mask, nested groups (nil blend = pass through), the merged composite, bitsPerChannel 8 or 16 and the embedded ColorProfile; LayerNode compares deep trees without recursion; CodecError (notThisFormat, damaged, unsupported, tooLarge, compressedEntry, pixelCodec). PixelCodec, the protocol apps plug their PNG codec into, with RawPixelCodec as the lossless test stand-in (a PNG signature and IHDR with its CRC, then Float32 components; depth 8 or 16, other bytes throw pixelCodec). ByteReader: big-endian and little-endian reads, each bounds checked (damaged), with length arithmetic that throws tooLarge on overflow, and the shared IEEE CRC-32 (slicing-by-8) that ZipStore and PNG use. PNG (PNGInfo, maxSide 30,000) and PNGCodec (the PixelCodec over PNG). PNG read (PNG, PNGRead): the signature (else notThisFormat), every chunk's CRC, IHDR first with sides within maxSide (tooLarge) and a depth its colour type allows, the area within PixelBuffer.maxPixels before anything is inflated or allocated, PLTE for palette images, tRNS as palette alpha or a grey or RGB key colour made transparent, ancillary chunks (gAMA, cHRM, iCCP, text) ignored and an unknown critical chunk unsupported; the joined IDATs inflated to exactly the filtered bytes IHDR implies, the five filters undone in place (Paeth ties to a, then b), Adam7 or one pass, 1-, 2-, 4-, 8- and 16-bit samples, sRGB decoded to linear through PSD's tables and premultiplied; a bad CRC, filter type, palette index or short stream damaged. PNG write (PNGWrite): unpremultiplied sRGB RGBA at 8 bits (DisplayBytes) or 16 (big-endian, PSD's linear table), other depths unsupported and sides over maxSide tooLarge; each row filtered (None, Sub, Up, Average, Paeth) by the least sum of absolute signed bytes, ties to the lower type; Deflate.zlib at the given level; IHDR (colour type 6, the depth), IDATs of at most 64 KiB, IEND, each with its CRC-32; PNGCodec.encodePNG wraps any refusal as pixelCodec. JPEG read (JPEG, JPEGDecode): JPEGInfo (size, components, progressive, EXIF orientation 1...8 in either byte order) from the markers; baseline and extended Huffman frames at 8 bits, grey or YCbCr at any factors 1...4 (box upsampled), DQT at 8 or 16 bits, restart intervals resetting the DC predictions, a float inverse DCT, JFIF YCbCr to RGB and DisplayTransfer's sRGB decode to linear premultiplied pixels with alpha 1, not rotated; SOF sides within maxSide (30,000) and PixelBuffer.maxPixels before any allocation (tooLarge), arithmetic, lossless, hierarchical, 12-bit, CMYK and DNL heights unsupported, and a bad marker, table or Huffman code or a short scan damaged. Progressive JPEG read (JPEGProgressive, T.81 Annex G): DC first and refinement scans, AC spectral selection with end-of-band runs and AC successive approximation refinement into the same coefficients the baseline scan fills, each scan's band and Ah/Al checked against what earlier scans coded (damaged otherwise), EOBRUN and the DC predictions reset at each restart, the coefficient store bounded by 384 blocks per byte left before allocation and all scans together by 64 visits per block (tooLarge). JPEG write (JPEGWrite): baseline JFIF 1.02 at quality 1...100 (else unsupported, sides over maxSide tooLarge): un-premultiplied then alpha dropped, DisplayTransfer's sRGB bytes, JFIF YCbCr, 4:2:0 box-averaged with edge replication, the K.1 and K.2 tables scaled by quality (5000/q below 50, else 200-2q, entries 1...255), a float forward DCT over the decoder's cosines, the K.3 to K.6 Huffman tables, one interleaved scan with 0xFF stuffed. Inflate (zlib and raw, RFC 1950 and 1951): stored, fixed and dynamic Huffman blocks through a 10-bit lookup table with a canonical walk for longer codes, the Adler-32 checked, damaged on a bad header (method, window, check bits, a preset dictionary), block type, stored length, over-subscribed or incomplete code, distance past the output or early end, tooLarge before the output would pass the limit. Deflate (Deflate, DeflateHuffman; zlib header 0x78 0x01, the Adler-32 last): stored blocks of at most 65,535 bytes at level 0; at 1...9 (others act as the nearest end) LZ77 over a 32 KiB window, hash chains of 3-byte prefixes searched as the level sets (4 << (level - 1) links, a quarter once a match reaches the good length, stopping at the nice length; lazy matching from level 4), into blocks of at most 32,768 symbols, each written stored, fixed or dynamic Huffman by an exact bit count, whichever is smallest; a dynamic block's codes are length-limited (15 bits, 7 for the code-length code, ties by symbol) and its header trims HLIT, HDIST and HCLEN and run-length codes the lengths with symbols 16, 17 and 18; deterministic. PackBits: header 0...127 copies n+1 literal bytes, -127...-1 repeats the next byte 1-n times, -128 is skipped; a run past the row's end or input that ends first throws damaged; the encoder writes runs of 3 or more as repeat packets, no packet over 128 bytes. ZipStore, the stored-only zip container: archive writes deterministic bytes (the first path, e.g. mimetype, at offset 30, the rest sorted by UTF-8, DOS date 0x0021, IEEE CRC-32), throwing unsupported for an empty name or a missing first and tooLarge past 65,535 entries or name bytes or 4 GiB sizes and offsets; entries throws compressedEntry for a compressed entry, unsupported for an encrypted one, damaged for a bad CRC, a repeated path, local and central sizes that differ or entry sizes summing past the archive's bytes, and notThisFormat without an end record. PSD read (PSD, PSDRead, PSDDeep): 8BPS version 1 (version 2 unsupported), 1...56 channels, 8 or 16 bits, RGB or grayscale (others unsupported), the ICC profile from resource 1039 (one ColorProfile refuses is dropped), raw and RLE channels (zip unsupported), layer masks, 16 blend keys (unknown reads normal), luni names, lsct groups, the merged image decoded as colour and one alpha only; limits maxSide 30,000 per side, maxLayers 8,000 records, maxDepth 256 nested groups and maxTotalPixels (PixelBuffer.maxPixels) summed over the canvas, every layer and every mask from the record bounds before any channel is decoded, all tooLarge. PSD write (PSDWrite, PSDDeep): 8 or 16 bits, RGB or grayscale under a gray profile, the profile as resource 1039, every channel RLE, a negative layer count, each group a bounding divider then a folder record, luni names, blend keys and the merged image (from composite, or flattened from the visible layers when it is nil); validated before any byte is written: opacity and mask default finite in 0...1 and a composite the canvas size (unsupported), canvas and record sides within maxSide, bounds within Int32, records within maxLayers and summed areas within maxTotalPixels (tooLarge). It has no nesting cap, so groups deeper than maxDepth write and PSD read refuses them. OpenRaster read (OpenRaster, StackXML, OpenRasterDeep): mimetype exactly image/openraster, stack.xml at most 16 MiB parsed by StackXML (nested stacks as groups within maxDepth, the root the first; layers and stacks within maxLayers; canvas within maxSide and PixelBuffer.maxPixels; x and y integers within 2^30 either way, else damaged; opacity clamped to 0...1, non-finite damaged; svg composite ops, unknown reads normal; entities decoded), a repeated or missing src damaged, every layer PNG and mergedimage.png sized from its IHDR and summed within maxTotalPixels before any is decoded once through the PixelCodec, a merged image other than the canvas size damaged, 16 bits when any IHDR says 16, and profile.icc within maxProfileBytes (16 MiB; a refused profile is dropped). OpenRaster write (OpenRasterWrite, OpenRasterDeep): stack.xml top first, one PNG per layer through the PixelCodec, mergedimage.png, a thumbnail 256 on its longest side (never scaled up), profile.icc and app extra entries; validated before anything is encoded: depth 8 or 16, a composite the canvas size, no mask or clipping, no NUL in a name, no extra entry on a standard or layer path (unsupported), sizes, offsets, counts and nesting within what the reader accepts. A group's isOpen is not kept. PixelBuffer profile conversion (ProfileConvert: unpremultiply, source curve, matrix, target curve, alpha and alpha-0 pixels kept, no clamp, a non-finite result throws), its curve passes read from per-channel lookup tables (ProfileConvertCurves, linear interpolation checked against the exact curve when built, with values outside the tables taking the exact path).

containers.name: CoreAsset library
containers.description: Shared asset module (Sources/CoreAsset): the Asset and AssetRef model every app imports and exports, and its manifest.json codec. Linux-safe, Foundation only, no dependencies.

components.name: Asset Model
components.description: Asset (id, kind, name, tags, version, source app, payload ref), AssetRef (id, version) and the manifest codec with size limits; AssetError.

components.name: Thumbnail Store
components.description: ThumbnailStore, the disk preview store: opaque encoded preview bytes (it never decodes images, and CoreAsset never imports CoreRaster) keyed by PreviewKey (asset, content token, SizeClass of 256, 1024 or 2560 px), each PreviewEntry naming its optional VolumeRef and relative path, and Availability (online, or offline with the volume). PreviewFiles is the layout: index.json, index.journal and p/<2 hex>/<16 hex>.bin files named by a 64-bit FNV-1a of the key, so no user text reaches a path; each file is FLPV, a version byte, a 4-byte big-endian length and that much JSON header naming its key, volume and path, then the payload. Every change runs under an exclusive flock on the folder's lock file and replaces a file by writing <name>.tmp whole, then renaming it over the old one. A write evicts the entry read longest ago (ties: the larger size class) while the payload bytes exceed the budget; opening a store never evicts. A read checks that the file's header names its key, returns nil and drops the entry when the file is gone, and bumps lastRead in memory; bumps are flushed with the next change, by the first read 2 s or more after the last flush, and on deinit, merged with the index on disk. PreviewJournal appends only the entries a change touched (FLPJ1:, the index's 16-hex generation, a newline, then one JSON put or drop per line); each store catches up on the lines others appended, ignores an unfinished last line and a journal of another generation, and compacts into a new snapshot past max(64, entries / 2) records, so index I/O per write is O(1) amortised. PreviewIndex is the snapshot codec (version 2; a version 1 index still loads) and its recovery: an index that fails to decode, names another version or an impossible size, or whose journal has a damaged line is renamed to index.damaged.json (its journal to index.damaged.journal, both kept) and rebuilt from the files: key, volume and path from each header, byteCount from the payload, lastRead from the modification date; a file whose header doesn't decode or that sits under another key's name is skipped and left on disk. Opening also deletes orphan .tmp files and drops entries whose file is gone. OfflineVolumes never probes the file system: the caller passes the mounted volume ids; entries(on:) matches by volume id alone, so a renamed volume keeps its entries; an entry whose volume id is not mounted reports offline while its bytes still read, and an entry with no volume is always online. Limits: the budget counts payloads only, not headers or the index; a negative budget throws; every failure is an AssetError; volume and duplicate facts beyond the entries belong to the catalog once its schema lands.

containers.name: CoreCatalog library
containers.description: Shared catalog module (Sources/CoreCatalog): photo and metadata catalog over SQLite, used by Library and the shared asset library. Linux-safe; depends only on GRDB.

components.name: Catalog Store
components.description: The catalog schema and its migrations, record types and queries (smart collection rules compiled to SQL) over a GRDB database; CatalogError, which GRDB's errors map to.

containers.name: CoreRender library
containers.description: Shared render module (Sources/CoreRender): the RenderBackend contract every app's Model draws through, its backends (a fake for tests, and the CPU backend over CoreRaster, the pixel reference), RenderDispatcher, which routes each op to a backend by support and health, the parity harness, and the Linux-safe parts of the Metal backend (capabilities, tiling math, cache keys). Linux-safe, Foundation only.

components.name: Render Contract
components.description: The RenderBackend contract: the op families (RenderOp), with the four CPU-first W1 families (maskedComposite, affine, effect, color) listed in RenderOp.notOnMetalYet, the one error type (RenderError), surface handles (RenderSurface), the tone adjustments the adjust and color families take (ToneAdjustment, whose family says which gates each case), the RenderBackend protocol with a not-on-this-backend default for each W1 method that throws unsupported with its family, the blend-mode-to-family and raster-error mappings every backend shares, the SurfaceStore that holds a backend's PixelBuffers behind one lock and updates one in place, the resident-rendering methods (blank and the batched composite of CompositeSteps, each with a default built from the older methods) and ResidentSurfaces, the layer tiles kept on a backend across renders keyed by layer and tile and uploaded only when their pixel storage changes (a written tile; the check is storage identity, so equal pixels in new storage upload again), ToneRendering, a backend that runs a whole ToneProgram over a surface in one pass (the CPU backend conforms through ToneProgram.map, the parity reference), and FakeBackend, the recording test double.

components.name: CPU Backend
components.description: CPUBackend, the CPU RenderBackend and pixel reference (Sources/CoreRender/CPU), supporting every op family: its surfaces are PixelBuffers held in the shared SurfaceStore; surface, read and release go through the SurfaceStore; display and composite (every blend mode, gated by its family) are the CoreRaster calls themselves, composite blending the stored backdrop in place under the store's lock so composites onto one surface apply one at a time, and crop, rotate, resample, blur, unsharp, each tone adjustment and masked clone (CPUBackend+Ops) each call the CoreRaster method they name and return a new surface. CoreRaster errors map to RenderError.raster with the same message. Each W1 family answers from its own file, CPUBackend+MaskedComposite, +Affine, +Effect and +Color (the color tone cases, reached from adjusted's switch). +Color is built: each color case calls the CoreRaster op it names (vibrance to invert, the LUT applied once) with no color math of its own. +Affine is filled: transformed and flipped call the CoreRaster ops into a new surface, and composite through a matrix runs CoreRaster's through-composite on the stored backdrop in place under the store's lock, as composite does. +Effect is filled: every LayerEffect is CoreRaster's applying(_:) on the surface's pixels, returned as a new surface. +MaskedComposite is filled: the masked composite runs CoreRaster's masked composite on the stored backdrop in place under the store's lock, as composite does. Every W1 family is now built.

components.name: Render Dispatcher
components.description: RenderDispatcher, the routing between backends: each op goes to the preferred backend when it supports the op's family and is healthy, else to the CPU backend, recording the last fallback (op family and reason, unsupported or unhealthy). A surface made by the other backend is read and re-uploaded to the routed backend first, so a fallback never changes a pixel. Each W1 method routes by its own family: the masked composite by maskedComposite whatever its blend mode, transformed, flipped and the composite through a matrix by affine, applying by effect, and each tone adjustment by ToneAdjustment.family (adjust or color); the two W1 composites move a backdrop the way composite does. The batched composite runs on one backend: the preferred one when every step's family routes there, else the CPU.

components.name: Metal Support
components.description: The Metal backend's Linux-safe parts (Sources/CoreRender/Metal): binary16 half-float conversion for filling rgba16Float textures from Float32 buffers and reading them back; MetalCapabilities, the proven op set and health state that RenderDispatcher reads, with the families still compiling in the background held out of its effective supports and the CPU-first families in RenderOp.notOnMetalYet never enabled; SurfaceTiling, the 256 px tile grid a surface's textures follow, on CoreRaster's shared tile math, with the tiles a rect touches, the default memory budget (half the working set, at least one tile) and wholeImageFits, the overflow-checked whole-image buffer-limit check that blur, unsharp and retouch call (w x h x 16 bytes against the device's maxBufferLength); PipelineKey, the identity of one cached compute pipeline (op family plus a short identifier variant) and the kernel function name it maps to; DisplayTable, CoreColor's DisplayTransfer byte rules as Float thresholds (the curve's and the alpha's, plus CoreColor's own linear sRGB to Display P3 matrix, DisplayTransfer.p3FromLinearSRGB, as Float) that the Metal display kernel uploads, with encode, the kernel's per-pixel rule in Swift, outputFits, display's check against the device's buffer limit, and the CPU backend's error for a non-display space; and TileMap, the pixel map of a crop or quarter turn between two tilings (crop rectangles checked with CoreRaster's messages) split into tile-to-tile copy pieces, refusing a tiling of another size than the source it was made for; and CompositeMap, the overlap of a source placed on a backdrop at an integer offset (CoreRaster's in-place composite clip, safe for any Int offset) split into tile-to-tile pieces, with CoreRaster's opacity check; and ResampleTable, one resample axis's taps (CoreRaster's public ResampleFilter.taps, clamp-to-edge indices and weights normalised in Double, flattened and stored as Float, the identity for an unchanged length) as flat arrays the Metal resample kernel uploads, with apply, the kernel's sum in Swift, and peakPixels, the largest buffer a resample allocates, checked against the device limit; and AdjustTable, every tone adjustment as CoreRaster's own adjustment on a probe line run through the CPU backend (per-channel gains for exposure and white balance, a square-root-spaced table over 0...1 with octave tables of the CPU's values outside it, 2^-24 to 2^40 on each side, read by exponent bits and interpolated on the mantissa, an overflowing octave holding the largest finite Float, for levels, curves and contrast, or a gain per Rec. 709 luminance, constant outside 0...1, for highlights/shadows) that the Metal adjust kernel uploads, with apply and map, the kernel's rule in Swift, and unsupported(.color) for every W1 colour case; and OpaqueRows, CoreRaster's opaque-row copy rule (.normal at opacity exactly 1, every stored alpha of the row exactly 1) as per-row flags of a composite piece split into maximal blit and kernel row runs; and BlurTable, CoreRaster's Gaussian blur kernel mirrored exactly (2 ceil(3 sigma) + 1 weights normalised in Double, stored as Float, sigma 0 the single weight 1, CoreRaster's sigma checks and messages, every weight pinned by test to CoreRaster's blur of an impulse) that the Metal blur kernel uploads, with apply, the kernel's clamp-to-edge sum in Swift; and UnsharpRule, the amount and threshold the Metal unsharp kernel uploads (as two Floats), with CoreRaster's amount, threshold and overflow checks and messages, and apply, the kernel's own Float32 rule per premultiplied component (a difference from the blur strictly over Float(threshold) moves it by amount times the difference, one fused multiply-add), which agrees with CoreRaster's Double rule to Float rounding, a difference that close to the threshold taking either branch; and ToneProgram, a chain of tone operations as the data one Metal pass reads (each adjustment's AdjustTable at its offset, hue/saturation as Float HSL, an app's 3x3 colour matrix with a lightness mix), with map, the kernel's rule in Swift. Pure Swift integer and floating-point math, no Metal import, so it builds, tests and mutates on Linux.

components.name: Parity Harness
components.description: How one RenderBackend is measured against another (Sources/CoreRender/Parity): ParityTolerance (byte and linear bounds, .standard and .nonSeparable); ParityHarness.compare, which checks two results' sRGB display bytes through CoreRaster's rgba8 and their linear premultiplied Floats over visible pixels and names the worst pixel; ParityHarness.compare(golden:), the bytes-only compare of a result against a golden, encoded in the golden's color space (both compares count only alpha where both alpha bytes are 0); ParityPack, the layout of the packed CPU goldens (ParityPack.all, each sample's band of rows) and ParityGolden.band(from:op:sample:) and rows(_:), which copy one sample's golden out of its pack; the deterministic sample set per RenderOp (seeded buffers plus alpha 0, subnormal alpha, opaque rows and sources off every edge) and rendering a sample on any backend, with one Samples+<Family>.swift file per W1 family (masked composite, affine, effect, color) giving that family's samples and packs (affine's ten samples through transformed, flipped and the composite through a matrix are in, one 9-wide pack; effect's twelve samples through applying, every LayerEffect case and a three-effect stack applied in turn, are in, one 9-wide pack; the masked composite's twelve, the four 9x7 sources through a feathered ellipse, that mask off each edge, a luminance and an inverted alpha matte, a full and an empty mask, all onto one 11x8 backdrop, are in, one 11-wide .standard pack; color's 44, one per colour ToneAdjustment case, LUT included, on each of the four 9x7 edge-case sources, one .standard pack); and golden files (raw rgba8 bytes beside a JSON header), validated as untrusted input.

containers.name: CoreRenderMetal library
containers.description: Metal render module (Sources/CoreRenderMetal): the Metal RenderBackend, macOS only. The one module allowed to import Metal; every file is wrapped in #if canImport(Metal), so Linux builds it empty.

components.name: Metal Backend
components.description: The Metal RenderBackend: a device and its command queue, capability state behind one lock that no GPU wait holds (fail; recover, which clears a failure only after the health probe passes on a new queue; a health probe that runs one kernel from its own memo; recordCompletion, which marks the backend unhealthy on any command-buffer error; a failed texture allocation also marks it unhealthy), tiled rgba16Float surfaces (one texture per 256 px tile, shared storage on unified memory and managed on a discrete GPU) uploaded from Float32 pixel buffers through HalfFloat with every component clamped to the finite half range and downloaded back, tile eviction under a memory budget (budgetBytes, half the device's recommended working set by default: the least recently used tiles move to a CPU shadow until residentBytes fits, and a read merges resident tiles with shadows), and the pipeline cache: MSL compiled at runtime from string constants, once per PipelineKey (variants from outside go through PipelineKey.validated), memoised in process with Metal's own shader cache across launches; cacheURL is reserved and nothing is read, written or deleted there. Display encode (MB-3, enabled at init) runs the display_encode kernel over resident tiles, reading DisplayTable's thresholds and P3 matrix, and encodes evicted tiles from their shadows on the CPU. Transform (MB-7) runs on the GPU: crop as blit copies and quarter turns as a rotate kernel, piece by piece from TileMap into a new surface (an evicted source tile is copied from its shadow through a temporary texture), with the CPU backend's errors for an invalid crop. Normal composite (MB-4, enabled at init on a read-write tier 2 device only) runs the composite_normal kernel in place on the backdrop's tiles, piece by piece from CompositeMap, with CoreRaster's sourceOver rule, opacity check and clip (an evicted backdrop tile is brought back to a texture first and the budget enforced after; a source that is the backdrop is read from a snapshot). The eleven other separable modes (MB-5) run as variants of the same in-place path, one blendSeparable_<mode> kernel each with CoreRaster's blend formula, with .blendSeparable enabled at init on a read-write tier 2 device (MB-6). Hue, saturation, color and luminosity (MB-9) run through the same in-place path as one blendNonSeparable_<mode> kernel each with CoreRaster's Lum, Sat, SetLum, SetSat and ClipColor, with .blendNonSeparable enabled at init on a read-write tier 2 device (MB-10). The opaque-row fast path (MB-6): under .normal at opacity exactly 1, the rows of a piece whose stored Float16 source alphas are all exactly 1 (read from the source tile, resident or staged) are copied onto the backdrop tile with blits instead of the kernel, split by OpaqueRows, with pixels equal to the CPU backend's copy. Resample (MB-8) runs bilinear and lanczos3 on the GPU as two separable passes of ResampleTable over whole-image float4 buffers in the CPU's pass order (the source read like `read`, resident tiles merged with shadows, and uploaded from the CPU), scattered into a new surface with components clamped to the finite half range; an invalid size throws the CPU backend's error, and a valid size whose largest buffer is over the device's maxBufferLength throws unsupported(.resample) with the backend still healthy, so the caller resamples on the CPU backend. Adjust (MB-13, MB-14; .adjust enabled at init) runs every tone adjustment (exposure, levels, curves, white balance, contrast, highlights/shadows) through the adjust_tone kernel tile by tile into a new surface, reading AdjustTable's per-channel gains, per-channel table with its two octave tables or luminance gain table on unpremultiplied values with CoreRaster's alpha guard (an evicted source tile through a temporary texture) and the CPU backend's errors for invalid parameters. Gaussian blur (MB-11) runs as two separable blur_pass passes of BlurTable over whole-image float4 buffers in the CPU's order (across, then down) with clamp-to-edge taps, scattered into a new surface by the resample scatter kernel; sigma 0 returns the pixels unchanged and an invalid sigma throws the CPU backend's error. Unsharp mask (MB-12) runs in one command buffer as blur_pass across the rows and then blur_unsharp, which finishes the blur down the columns and sharpens each premultiplied component in Float32 with UnsharpRule's parameters (the rule UnsharpRule.apply mirrors), scattered into a new surface; invalid parameters and an overflowing result throw the CPU backend's errors; .blur is enabled at init, and blur and unsharp throw unsupported while the backend is unhealthy and, with the backend still healthy, for a valid image whose whole-image buffer is over the device's maxBufferLength, so the caller runs them on the CPU backend. Clone through a mask (MB-15; .retouch enabled at init) packs the source, read like `read`, and the mask's coverage into whole-image buffers and runs retouch_clone into each tile of a new surface with CoreRaster's clone rule, the CPU backend's errors in its order, and offsets whose sources are all off the image returning the pixels unchanged; an image over maxBufferLength throws unsupported, and so does clone while the backend is unhealthy. Every family is enabled at init: display, transform, resample, adjust, blur and retouch on any device, and composite, blendSeparable and blendNonSeparable on a read-write tier 2 device only (elsewhere those modes throw unsupported). While the backend is unhealthy supports is empty and every op throws unsupported(<family>); with it healthy, display, resample, blur (gaussianBlur and unsharpMask) and retouch (cloned) throw unsupported(<family>) for a buffer over the device's maxBufferLength, leaving the backend healthy, so the caller runs the op on the CPU backend. A backend made with startingInBackground (MB-17) returns at once with every family it enables held in MetalCapabilities.compiling, so supports lacks them and their ops throw unsupported, and builds their built-in pipelines on a dispatch queue off the caller's, with the lock free, memoising each without replacing one already compiled on first use and releasing each family when done; a failed compile marks the backend failed and releases the family. The plain init compiles each pipeline on first use, under the lock. Resident rendering: blank surfaces filled from zeros, the batched composite of many steps in one command buffer committed with no wait (every later op on the queue is ordered after it, and a GPU failure marks the backend failed from its completion handler), uploads converted a row at a time through Float16, and display into a caller's rgba8 or bgra8 texture (straight or premultiplied) with no readback; display into that texture through a ToneProgram (display_tone) so a live adjustment is one pass over a resident picture, and ToneRendering's adjusted(_:tone:) (adjust_program), a whole program into a new surface.
